text.p: Prime Hospitality Corp sees $0.06 per share accretion in the first operating year per new AmeriSuites hotels and $0.08 per hotel in the second year, said Chief Financial Officer John Elwood.
Speaking at a Montgomery Securities Hospitality Conference in New York, Elwood said that 20 AmeriSuites hotels were opened last year bringing the total number to 39.
The company projects 69 AmeriSuites locations at the end of 1997.

Elwood also said that the company was implementing a central reservation system for its AmeriSuites chain which would provide enhanced data mining and guest history data and automatic linkage to other marketing systems.
He said the company sees a $0.01 to $0.02 EPS contribution from the new reservation system.
According to Chief Executive David Simon, the company sees high single digits or low double digits revenue-per-average-room (REVPAR) growth for the AmeriSuites in 1997.
He said that AmeriSuites had witness 16 percent REVPAR increase in 1996 but "we probably won't see that kind of growth this year."
Prime Hospitality is an independent lodging company that currently owns or operates about 100 hotel properties through out the United States.
The company's portfolio consists of hotels that bear its proprietary brand name AmeriSuites and Wellesley Inns, or are operated under franchise affiliation with national chains.
